items.title: SAP Porto 2026: The power of the SAP Community, Moshe Naveh
items.author: deiamolina
items.text:
This post is part of my SIT Porto 2026 series. Main post: SIT Porto 2026: A first time, and why I'll be back 
 The power of the SAP Community: Simplified Blogging and Personal Branding in the era of AI , by moshenaveh 
 Moshe Naveh is a Senior Community Manager and Advocate for the SAP Community, and he talked about authenticity in the AI era. Always friendly, with a smile on his face, Moshe showed how to use the community to the members' advantage. 
 Watch the talk: https://www.youtube.com/live/grU_TdxhjNY?t=1860s (starts at 0:31). 
 The DOM 
 The DOM (Document Object Model) is how a browser sees a web page: a tree where every title, paragraph and image is a branch. Here's the tree of this post: 
 <post> 
 ├── 1. Why this topic matters to me (and to everyone) 
 │ └── The importance of a non-technical talk in a technology community event 
 ├── 2. Summary of the talk (and my observations) 
 │ ├── Why blogging can be intimidating 
 │ ├── The influencer fallacy 
 │ ├── Simplified blogging 
 │ └── Special initiatives to follow 
 ├── 3. The most important part 
 ├── 4. A special thanks 
 └── 5. The sovereignty challenge (or António's challenge) 
 1. Why this topic matters to me (and to everyone) 
 This topic speaks to my heart. After 20+ years working with SAP, almost 15 of them at the same company, I had built a personal brand inside the company, and that is also why I wasn't part of the SAP Community before: my bubble was internal. While attending an Women's Leadership program, I noticed that, having a external personal brand and becoming more active in the SAP Community would be great not only for me but also for the company. I would be able to share my knowledge and learn a lot to become a better professional. So I started blogging here and how I was very interested on Moshe's presentation. 
 💡 Tip of the day: keep your presence internal and external even when you are not looking for new opportunities. It's the best way to keep yourself updated! The importance of a non-technical talk in a technology community event 
 This was the only talk focused purely on people and community. Many technical people might think this is not as important, but let me remind you, my friend: you are human, you work for humans, you live with humans and you love humans. We are, and should always be, the center of technology. 
 2. Summary of the talk (and my observations) 
 Moshe talked about how to be a valuable participant in the community and get the best out of it: 
 Explore and follow topics 
 Engage with the content 
 Write your own posts and answer questions 
 And with that, you build your personal brand! Why blogging can be intimidating 
 People are afraid of blogging for many reasons, and it can be intimidating even for me, and I love to write: 
 Thinking you don't know enough to share 
 Fear of writing something sensitive about your company (my rule: only publish public information) 
 Not having visibility 
 Concluding, when there are no interactions, that it wasn't worth it The influencer fallacy 
 I believe I have a lot to put on the table, and the presence to sit at the table. But when I post, I don't get 200 likes, and I won't lie: I felt discouraged. 
 And here is what I call the influencer fallacy. We are used to influencers who are famous, and people will like their posts no matter what they post. I don't post for the likes, and I need to remind myself of that all the time. I post to share knowledge and to make real connections. So please keep that in mind too. Simplified blogging 
 Some people are natural communicators and would talk to a wall if no one else were around (me). Others (my husband) have a lot of internal chats, but why bother making them more public? I promise you, when he talks I realize he has as much to say as I do. Those types usally get married hahaha 
 Everybody has opinions and can help others and enrich the community. EVERYBODY! 
 So, if writing is not natural to you, maybe talking is. Maybe talking out loud when you are alone? Great: Moshe found a way for you to put it out in the world, if you want to. 
 Simplified blogging is: create a template, record yourself with a transcript, create a blog post from it using a prompt, review, validate, remove the robot part of the text, review again, make it authentic, and publish! 
 Moshe gave an example: he records himself while walking and transforms it into blog posts. Honestly, I don't see myself doing it (for a reason you'll find in the sovereignty challenge below). I would rather sit down and write, but that's the beauty of life: one size doesn't fit all, and thank God it doesn't. Can you imagine a world with only one kind of person? Boring! 
 Don't forget to always be transparent when you use AI to help you write, check the content of your blog posts before publishing, be authentic, and remember you own your blogs. It's your reputation we are talking about. 
 Special initiatives to follow 
 Before I gave your the wrong directions, let me confirm with Moshe. I will update this post with the proper links, but the initiaves he mentioned are: 
 Hello SAP Community 
 SAP Community Hobbies series 
 Speaker series 
 3. The most important part 
 We do have AI and all today, but we are beautiful creatures with a head full of imagination. All of us, even if you don't realize it. Blogging is a beautiful way to unlock your creative self, and we need more humans and authenticity around 😉 
 4. A special thanks 
 A special thanks to Moshe, who was so open to talk and to help me unlock my blogging too. Thank you a million! 
 5. The sovereignty challenge (or António's challenge) 
 Remember I said I don't see myself recording my voice? Since I don't know where, when and how my data is processed on AI servers, I'm still a bit reluctant to upload my voice and pictures to it. But hey, I'm the cybersecurity-crazy one who puts tape over the phone camera. And before you think this is unsustainable today (and it is: we have cameras everywhere and microphones in our pockets), I still want the illusion that I can somehow control it. Let me be, please 😂 Or feel free to make jokes about me in the comments, I can handle it. 
 That's my take for my voice and pictures, but I do see huge value in these tools too. Maybe in the future, when regulations and laws protect us. I hope we get there soon 🤞

items.title: Building an MCP Server on Integration Cell part of SAP Integration Suite : APIs to AI Agents
items.author: nitesh_agrawal2
items.text:
Credit : In a series of super blogs, my colleague @Ashutosh_KSingh has explained how to set up Integration Cell, What is API Centric Integration and How to get started with MCP servers on Integration Suite. 
 https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-sap/api-centric-integration-on-sap-integration-suite-part-1-build-and-deploy/ba-p/14438357 
 https://community.sap.com/t5/integration-blog-posts/mcp-servers-on-sap-integration-suite-build-your-first-mcp-server-from-an/ba-p/14441034 
 This Blog post builds on this knowledge and works on a scenario comparing SuccessFactors API Consumption via Application vs Agents, powered by MCP servers on Integration Cell. 

 A New Way to Deliver HR Self-Service 
 It is 9 AM on a Monday. John Smith has just joined ABC Corp and is sitting through onboarding. The HR presenter mentions the Company Car benefit. 
 John wants to know what cars he can choose, which vendors are approved, what the lease rates look like, and whether he is already enrolled. The presenter points him to the employee portal. 
 John opens the portal. It does exactly what it was built to do — he finds a Car Options screen with approved models, vendors, and lease providers, and a second screen showing his enrollment status. The portal works well for the questions it was designed to answer. 
 Then John asks a follow-up: "Which provider gives me the best deal for a Toyota?" That one is not on any screen. He opens a helpdesk ticket and gets a reply two days later. 
 This is a familiar and reasonable situation. HR portals are purpose-built, well-governed, and take significant effort to deliver — typically 8 to 12 weeks. They serve the majority of employee needs well. The challenge is the long tail: every new question that was not anticipated at design time either goes unanswered or triggers a new development sprint. 
 This blog introduces a complementary approach — using Integration Cell, part of SAP Integration Suite's MCP capability to expose the same SuccessFactors APIs as AI agent tools, so that employees can ask questions in natural language and get answers beyond what any fixed screen provides. 

 Part 1: The Data Model — SuccessFactors Company Car APIs 
 Before building anything, it helps to understand what APIs we are working with. 
 SAP SuccessFactors exposes its benefits domain via OData v2. The Company Car benefit has six entities, arranged in three clean layers. 
 The Three Layers 
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Layer 1 — Reference Data │
│ ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │
│ │ AllowedModels │ │ RecommendedVendors │ │
│ │ Toyota, Nissan, VW │ │ Hertz, AVIS │ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────┘ │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ LeaseServiceProvider │ │
│ │ AVIS Rental (10.20%), LeasePlan │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 2 — Policy │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ BenefitCompanyCar │ │
│ │ Lock-in period, maintenance, buyback, EMI freq │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 3 — Employee Transactions │
│ ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │
│ │ CompanyCarEnrollment │ │ CompanyCarClaim │ │
│ │ John's enrollment │ │ John's claims │ │
│ └──────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 
 The full API spec is available on SAP API Business Accelerator Hub : https://hub.sap.com/api/ECGlobalBenefits/overview 

 Part 2: Building the MCP Server on SAP Integration Suite 
 SAP Integration Suite's Integration Cell runtime supports creating MCP servers directly from an OpenAPI specification — no custom code required. Here is how to set it up, step by step. 
 Step 1 — Get the OpenAPI Spec 
 Download the API spec from SAP API Business Accelerator Hub (search for "Global Benefits" ). The spec is in OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) format. 
 Important: Integration Suite's MCP server requires OpenAPI 3.0 . Use any AI tool (or the Swagger Converter) to upgrade the spec from 2.0 to 3.0 before proceeding. 

 Step 2 — Create an Integration Package 
 Log in to your Integration Suite tenant and navigate to Design → Integration Packages . Create a new integration package to hold your MCP server artifact. 
 Step 3 — Add an MCP Server Artifact 
 Inside the package, click Add → MCP Server . 

 In the creation wizard: 
 Select HTTP Endpoint with OpenAPI Specification as the connection type 
 Set Method to Upload 
 Upload your OpenAPI 3.0 spec file 
 Set the virtual host path — for example: <Virtual Host>/sfsf 

 This is where your MCP endpoint URL will be hosted. 
 Step 4 — Select Your Tools 
 After uploading the spec, the wizard discovers all available API paths as potential tools. Search for "Company Car" in the search field and select all 12 related tools. Click Add . 

 The MCP server artifact is now created. 

 Step 5 — Configure Tools, Prompts, and Resources 
 Open the MCP server artifact and switch to the MCP Configuration tab. You will see four sections: Source | Tools | Resources | Prompts . 

 Under Tools , you can: 
 View all selected tools 
 Add or remove tools 
 Click any tool to inspect its Input Schema and Output Schema 
 Edit tool names and descriptions in edit mode 
 Pro tip: Invest time in editing tool descriptions. The natural language description you write for each tool is what the AI agent reads when deciding which tools to call. A clear description like "Returns the list of car models the company has approved for the benefit program" is far more useful to an agent than "BenefitCompanyCarAllowedModels" . 
 Similarly, the Prompts and Resources sections can be enriched with additional context per the MCP specification. 
 Step 6 — Configure Policies 
 Click the Policies section to view what is applied to the MCP endpoint. 

 Authentication and Authorization are applied by default. 
 In the Authentication policy settings, add Basic authentication — this supports Process Integration Runtime (PIR) credentials, which is how agents will authenticate when calling the MCP server. OAuth (client credentials) and Client Certificate authentication are also supported. 

 For Authorization , keep the default settings. The scope API.invoke is required — the JWT token issued using PIR credentials already contains this scope. 

 Other policies — traffic management, IP filter — are available from the policy palette. We will cover these in a later article in this series. 

 Step 7 — Configure the Backend Connection 
 Before deploying, configure authentication for the SuccessFactors target endpoint. 
 Click on the HTTP receiver adapter and: 
 Set Authentication to Basic 
 Enter the Credential Name — for example, sfsf (a credential stored in the Security Material section of Integration Suite, containing your SuccessFactors username and password) 

 Step 8 — Deploy 
 Save the artifact and click Deploy . Select Integration Cell as the Runtime Profile. The virtual host will be pre-populated. 

 Once deployed, the artifact status changes to Deployed . 

 Step 9 — Grab the MCP Endpoint URL 
 Navigate to Monitor → Integrations and APIs , set Runtime to Integration Cell , and click the Manage Integration Content tile → Started . 
 Your MCP Server artifact appears at the top. The endpoint URL is visible in the right panel — this is the URL you will configure in any AI agent. 

 Part 3: Connecting an AI Agent 
 The MCP endpoint can be connected to any MCP-compatible AI client — Joule (SAP's own AI assistant), Claude Desktop, Cline, GitHub Copilot, and others. 
 Getting Credentials 
 The agent authenticates using Process Integration Runtime (PIR) service key credentials. These are the same credentials used to invoke Integration Flows — retrieve them from the service key of your PIR instance on SAP BTP. 

 Connecting Joule 
 In this demo we use Joule Work Desktop — SAP's generative AI assistant and agent orchestrator. Joule supports external MCP server connections. 

 Once connected, Joule discovers all 12 tools exposed by the MCP server automatically. No further configuration is needed — the agent is ready to reason. 

 Connecting Claude / Cline 
 For Claude Desktop or Cline, the MCP configuration looks like this: 
 { 
 "mcpServers" : { 
 "sfsf-company-car" : { 
 "type" : "http" , 
 "url" : "https://<virtual-host>/sfsf" , 
 "headers" : { 
 "Authorization" : "Basic <base64-encoded-pir-credentials>" 
 } 
 } 
 } 
 } 

 Part 4: The Experience — John Meets His AI Agent 
 ABC Corp has deployed the MCP server. John opens his AI assistant and types his questions exactly as he would ask a colleague. 
 Question 1 — "What are my car options?" 
 "I'm an employee looking to enroll in the company car benefit. What car models can I choose from, which vendors are recommended, and what lease service providers are available?" 
 The agent reasons silently and calls three tools in parallel: get_allowed_car_models , get_recommended_vendors , get_lease_providers . 
 Agent responds — 
 Hi John! Here's what your company car benefit offers: 
 Approved Models: Toyota, Nissan, Volkswagen 
 Approved Vendors: Hertz, AVIS 
 Lease Financing: Provider Monthly EMI Rate 
 AVIS Rental 10.20% 
 LeasePlan Contact HR for rate 
 Installments are paid monthly. Let me know if you'd like details on policy terms! 

 We can see the conversation with Joule and the tool calls it made on the right side. 

 Question 2 — "What is my enrollment and claim status?" 
 "Can you show me the current company car benefit policies, my enrollment details, and whether I have any open claims?" 
 The agent calls get_car_benefit_policy , get_employee_car_enrollment , and get_employee_car_claims in parallel. 
 Agent responds: 
 Policy: Three active car benefit policies, all with monthly installment frequency. 
 Your Enrollment: You have an active enrollment (ID: 163585), but it is incomplete — your car model, vendor, and EMI amount have not been selected yet. 
 Claims: No claims on file. 
 Next step: Complete your enrollment by selecting a model and a financing option. Want help comparing them? 

 The Follow-up — Where the Agent Extends Beyond the Portal 
 "Which lease provider gives me the best deal if I go with a Toyota?" 
 This question sits outside what the portal was designed to show — it would normally mean a helpdesk ticket and a future sprint. 
 With the MCP agent, no new development is needed. The agent re-reads the lease provider and policy data already retrieved: 
 The only provider currently showing a configured EMI rate is AVIS Rental at 10.20% — LeasePlan's rate is not yet set in the system. For a Toyota, AVIS Rental is your best available option. I'd recommend confirming the exact monthly EMI with HR, since it depends on the car's purchase value. 

 Zero development. Zero tickets. Answered in seconds. 

 Part 5: Portal and Agent — Better Together 
 The portal and the MCP agent are not competing approaches — they serve different needs. The portal delivers a reliable, governed, designed experience for the majority of employee interactions. The agent handles the long tail: the follow-up question, the cross-entity comparison, the query no one thought to build a screen for. 
 Architecture Comparison 
 HR Portal: 
 John opens the portal
 │
 ▼
IT-built portal backend
 ├── API call 1 → AllowedModels
 ├── API call 2 → RecommendedVendors
 ├── API call 3 → LeaseServiceProvider
 ├── API call 4 → BenefitCompanyCar
 ├── API call 5 → CompanyCarEnrollment
 └── API call 6 → CompanyCarClaim
 │
 ▼
 JOIN logic in backend
 │
 ▼
 Designed screen renders the data
 │
 ▼
 John gets a reliable, consistent answer
 for questions the portal was built to answer 
 MCP Agent: 
 John's natural language question
 │
 ▼
AI Agent (Joule / Claude / Cline)
 │
 ▼
MCP Server on SAP Integration Suite
 ├── get_allowed_car_models ──→ SF OData

items.title: Releasing SAC Pilot: The Ultimate Productivity Browser Extension for SAP Analytics Cloud
items.author: rohitchouhan
items.text:
If you build stories, write analytical scripts, configure planning simulations, or manage models inside SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), you know the daily friction all too well: 
 You are deep in the middle of designing a critical dashboard or calculation, and you need to look up a specific Cost Center code, Hierarchy parent node, or Dimension Member ID. 
 You have to navigate completely away from your active story canvas or launch an entirely separate browser tab. 
 The SAC Modeler takes 30 to 60 seconds to boot up its heavy menus, breaking your concentration and flow. 
 You only wanted a quick master data export or a clean CSV extract of fact data, but you were forced to step through a multi-step export wizard. 
 Transporting stories between Development, QA, and Production environments often breaks unexpectedly because a single dimension member was missing or had different attributes across tenants. 
 We built SAC Pilot to eliminate this friction once and for all. It is an independent, 100% client-side browser extension that sits pinned right inside your browser's native side panel, auto-detects your active SAP Analytics Cloud session, and helps you work faster without ever leaving your canvas. 
 What is SAC Pilot? 

 SAC Pilot is an open-community, high-performance browser extension crafted specifically for SAC Story Designers, Planners, BI Consultants, and Enterprise Architects. It operates directly alongside your active SAP Analytics Cloud workspace across Google Chrome (recommended), Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and Mozilla Firefox . 
 Unlike traditional add-ons or middleware that require server installations, database connections, or complicated OAuth setup, SAC Pilot uses a Zero-Configuration, Zero-Trust architecture. It securely senses your existing, authenticated browser session cookie and directly queries the tenant's REST and OData APIs over HTTPS. 
 Key Features & Capabilities 
 SAC Pilot packs over 15+ specialized power tools and utilities into a single, cohesive side-panel interface: 
 1. Instant Model & Data Provider Browser 
 Features type-ahead autocomplete search across all Analytical Models, Planning Models, and Data Providers configured within your tenant. You can view technical model IDs, descriptions, and data source metadata instantly, and switch between models in a single click without page reloads. 
 2. Dimension Member & Hierarchy Tree Explorer 
 Look up dimension member IDs, descriptions, and custom property attributes in sub-seconds. Explore complex parent-child hierarchy trees with interactive rollup expansion, allowing you to trace drill-down levels and aggregation paths on the fly. 
 3. High-Throughput Fact Data Exporter 
 Stream millions of transactional fact records directly from SAC models at blazing speeds (up to 100,000+ records per second) with live throughput progress indicators and time-remaining estimates. Download pristine CSV or JSON extracts ready for Microsoft Excel, Python, or data pipelines. 
 4. Reverse CSV Fact Data Importer 
 Upload external CSV datasets directly back into your SAC planning models without opening backend data integration wizards. The tool maps columns, validates schemas, and pushes records directly into the model. 
 5. Visual Column & Measure Filter Builder 
 Construct complex OData query filters visually before downloading data. Filter by dimension members, posting periods, version tags, or numerical measure ranges to retrieve only the exact dataset slice you need. 
 6. Planning Version Manager (Edit, Copy & Publish) 
 Inspect both Public and Private planning versions at a glance. Review version publication states, ownership, and creation timestamps. Trigger one-click data publishing, create version copies, and manage planning simulations effortlessly. 
 7. User & Team Inspector (SCIM Governance) 
 Audit and search tenant users, email directories, assigned roles, and security teams without needing full SAC Administration menu access. Perfect for validating permissions and verifying user provisioning. 
 8. Currency Exchange Rate Inspector 
 Instantly inspect Currency Conversion Tables configured on your tenant. Review exchange rate types, source and target currency pairs, and effective date validity ranges without opening Modeler settings. 
 9. Multi-Tenant Comparator (Dev vs. QA vs. Prod) 
 Compare dimension structures and member records between two different SAC tenant environments. The diff engine flags synced members, attribute differences, and missing members in the target tenant, helping you catch missing master data before transporting stories. 
 10. Synthetic Mock Test Data Generator 
 Automatically generate structured, realistic mock transactional fact data matching your model's exact dimension schemas. Configure cardinality, random distributions, and date ranges to stage models for testing and demonstration. 
 11. In-Panel Visualizer & Analytics 
 Embedded Chart.js analytics right inside the extension panel. Render instant bar charts, measure distribution curves, and member cardinality breakdowns without needing to create disposable story widgets. 
 12. Smart Bookmarks & Saved Filter Queries 
 Bookmark your most frequently accessed models, dimensions, and custom filter configurations. Jump straight into your daily operational views with one click. 
 13. 1-Click Clipboard Utilities 
 Copy individual member IDs, formatted string arrays, or JSON arrays directly to your system clipboard, formatted specifically for pasting into SAC story calculation scripts, advanced formulas, or SQL queries. 
 14. Public Dimensions Explorer 
 Dedicated inspection view for tenant-wide shared Public Dimensions, allowing you to audit global master data independent of individual analytical models. 
 15. Application Audit Logs Explorer 
 Inspect model application audit logs and change histories directly within the extension to audit updates and track modifications. 
 16. Deep Link Story & Modeler Navigator 
 Generate one-click direct deep links to navigate straight to the exact model or story in the native SAC interface. 
 Feature Overview Table 

 Feature Category Tool Name Primary Benefits Target User 
 Data Export High-Throughput Fact Exporter Stream fact data at 100k+ rows/sec to CSV/JSON BI Analysts & Data Engineers 
 Data Import Reverse CSV Importer Push external fact datasets into models Planners & Data Modelers 
 Master Data Dimension & Hierarchy Explorer Instant member search & parent-child tree drill-down Story Designers & Planners 
 Planning Version Manager Review, copy, and publish planning versions in 1 click Financial Planners 
 Governance User & Team Inspector SCIM audit of users, roles, and teams Administrators & Leads 
 Quality Assurance Tenant Comparator Diff dimensions across Dev, QA, and Prod Release Managers & Architects 
 Testing Test Data Generator Generate synthetic mock facts based on model schema Model Developers & Testers 
 Finance Currency Table Inspector Audit conversion rates and currency pairs Financial Controllers 
 Productivity Smart Bookmarks & Clipboard Save frequent queries and copy arrays for scripting All SAC Users 
 Security AES-256 GCM Storage Vault Zero-trust, client-side encryption of all local caches Security & Compliance Teams 
 Zero-Trust Architecture & Enterprise Security 
 Enterprise data privacy is non-negotiable. SAC Pilot was designed from the ground up to comply with strict enterprise IT security standards: 
 100% Client-Side Operation: The extension operates entirely within your local browser. There are no intermediate proxy servers, cloud relays, or backend databases. 
 Direct HTTPS Communication: Every network call is dispatched directly between your browser and your authenticated SAC tenant domain. 
 No Telemetry or Tracking: SAC Pilot collects zero personal information, logs no tenant activity, and includes no third-party tracking scripts. 
 AES-256 GCM Encrypted Vault: Any data persisted locally (such as bookmarks and cached dimension names) is encrypted using the browser's native Web Crypto API before being written to storage. 
 Session Cookie Inheritance: SAC Pilot never asks for, stores, or handles your password. It relies entirely on your browser's existing authenticated SAC session cookie. 
 Instant Data Purge: A dedicated single-click "Wipe Storage" option in the Settings panel allows you to instantly purge all stored keys, bookmarks, and local data. 
 How to Install & Get Started 
 You can install SAC Pilot directly from the official portal: 
 Official Installation Website: sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com 
 Easy 3-Step Installation: 
 Go to sac-pilot.rohitchouhan.com in your browser. 
 Click the install button for your browser (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, or Mozilla Firefox). 
 Confirm the prompt to add the extension to your browser. 
 Getting Started in 60 Seconds: 
 Log in to your regular SAP Analytics Cloud tenant. 
 Open SAC Pilot by clicking the extension icon in your browser toolbar or opening your browser's native Side Panel. 
 The extension automatically detects your active authenticated SAC session — no API keys, logins, or configurations needed. 
 Select any tool from the Home screen (such as Data Export/Import , Dimension Explorer , or Version Manager ) and start exploring your data right beside your active stories. 
 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) 
 Does SAC Pilot require an API key, Login Credentials or SAC OAuth client setup? 
 No. SAC Pilot automatically uses your existing authenticated browser session cookies to interact with SAC's standard endpoints. No administrator API configuration is required. 
 Can SAC Pilot see or transmit my company's data? 
 Never. SAC Pilot runs 100% inside your client browser. It never connects to any external third-party server. All data stays strictly between your browser and your company's official SAC tenant. 
 Does it support both Classic and New Planning Models? 
 Yes. SAC Pilot supports Analytical Models, Classic Account Models, and the New Model (Measure-based) type. 
 Is SAC Pilot free to use? 
 Yes, SAC Pilot is an open-community tool designed to give back to the SAP Analytics Cloud ecosystem. 
 Legal Disclaimer & Trademark Notice 
 Please review the following legal disclosures regarding SAC Pilot: 
 Not an Official SAP Extension: SAC Pilot is an independent third-party project created by Rohit Chouhan. It is not developed, tested, certified, maintained, supported, or endorsed by SAP SE. 
 Trademark Ownership: SAP, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP HANA, SAP BTP, and other SAP products and services mentioned herein, as well as their respective logos, are trademarks or registered trademarks of SAP SE in Germany and other countries worldwide. All other company, product, and service names used are for identification purposes only and belong to their respective owners. 
 Independent Companion Tool: This tool is created independently as an open-community utility for SAP Analytics Cloud practitioners to improve productivity. 
 No Official Affiliation: Reference to SAP Analytics Cloud does not imply any affiliation with or endorsement by SAP SE. The official SAP website is located at https://www.sap.com . 
 Warranty & Compliance: This software is provided on an "as-is" basis without warranties of any kind. Users are responsible for adhering to their organization's internal data governance and security policies when handling corporate tenant data. 
 Conclusion 
 SAC Pilot transforms the way professionals interact with SAP Analytics Cloud by removing friction, accelerating daily tasks, and providing deep data visibility right beside your active work. Whether you are validating a single dimension member, streaming a million fact records, or diffing master data across enterprise environments, SAC Pilot is your trusted companion.

items.title: Unable to Import/Execute Dynamic Parameter in SAC
items.author: paul_theconsultant
items.text:
I am working on developing an AR Aging Report from the ground up. The report will include sales-related filters such as Product, Sales Organization, Distribution Channel etc. I am using I_ARAgingGridGenLedgerCube and I_GLAccountLineItemCube as the primary and associated data sources, respectively with the intention of importing the resulting data into SAC. 
 However, I am encountering the following error: 
 The user doesn't have permission to access the requested resource. 
 Correlation ID: 6696200273784954a152783886829908 
 This error appears to point to a specific restriction (400/403 Permission Error) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when standard cubes are bundled into a custom view - Headless technical communication users appear to be restricted from executing dynamic parameters through OData V2 paths ( / Results ) on financial ledger structures. 
 Below are the steps I followed in an attempt to work around the error: 
 I created my first Custom CDS View using the Standard View scenario. I selected the required elements and created a dynamic date placeholder (ZSnapshotDateField) for the P_KeyDate parameter. For P_OverdueInterval 1-6 and P_FutureDueInterval 1-3, I manually entered constant values. 
 I repeated the above process by creating another Custom CDS View using the Analytical Cube scenario. 
 I then repeated the process by wrapping the cube using the External API scenario. 
 I proceeded to configure the Custom Communication Scenarios and Communication Arrangement, and created a connection to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition using the connection profile generated from the process above. 
 In SAC, under New Query for SAP S/4HANA, I selected Freehand Query and entered the following: 
 YY1_AGINGANALYSISCUBE4API_CDS;v=0002/YY1_AgingAnalysisCube4API(P_KeyDate=datetime'2026-10-03')/Results 
 When I follow the same process without the P_KeyDate parameter , the data is successfully imported into SAC using the ‘Build a Query’ option in the New Query for SAP S/4HANA window. 
 The issue therefore appears to be specifically related to the use of the ‘P_KeyDate’ parameter in the OData request, rather than the underlying Custom CDS View, Analytical Cube, External API configuration or SAC connection itself.

items.title: Agentic AI on BTP: Chaining Agents into a Workflow
items.author: WouterLemaire
items.text:
Introduction 
 An orchestrator that decides at runtime which specialist to call is great in a chat. At 04:23 in the morning, with nobody watching, it is the last thing you want. 
 This is the third post in the series, after configuring an agent ( https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-members/agentic-ai-on-btp-configuring-code-based-agents-on-the-fly/ba-p/14488352 ) and running it on a schedule ( https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-members/agentic-ai-on-btp-running-your-agents-unattended-on-a-schedule/ba-p/14493817 ). 
 In this blog post, I’ll show you the piece I kept teasing in both: workflows. Agents chained in a declared line, configured the same way, still no redeploy. 
 Problem 
 My first scheduled mail triage was one agent with a very long instruction. Read the mailbox, classify, look it up, draft a reply. It worked. Mostly. 
 The first set of problems was all the same problem: the model decided the path. 
 On a busy morning it read twelve messages and handled four, because nothing forced it to loop. 
 A retry after a failure started over and re-drafted replies it had already written. 
 When it went wrong, the only record was a wall of text. 
 Next to that, one agent doing everything carries a second cost: 
 Too many tools. Mail, SAP and documentation on one agent is a long tool list. The longer that list, the more often it reaches for the wrong one. 
 One model for every step. Reading a dump and classifying it is not the same job as reasoning about a fix. Both ran on the expensive model. 
 More access than the task needs. The step that writes the mail has no business holding a connection to the SAP system. 
 Not every step needs a model at all. Picking a branch on a status, pulling a field out of JSON, calling an endpoint: that is logic, not judgement. Running it through an LLM makes it slower, more expensive and less predictable. 
 What I wanted instead is specialized agents, each with only the tools for its own job and a model that matches the complexity of that job. A cheap reader up front, an expensive specialist where it earns its keep and a mail writer that holds no SAP access of its own. And where a step is plain logic, no agent at all, so AI and deterministic code sit in the same line. 
 The orchestrator has a job in the chat and does it well. It is simply the wrong tool for a nightly run, where the value is in doing the same thing every time. 
 Solution 
 A workflow is a row with branches and steps under it, exactly like an agent is a row with toolsets under it. Create it in the admin UI, reload, it runs. The definition is the authority: no model reorders or skips a step. 

 Under the hood the workflow runner mirrors the agent run path from the previous post, same background task handling, same overlap lock, same shutdown behaviour. What is different is the shape. 
 Main line, fan-out, branches, join 
 A workflow has one main line of steps. One of them can be marked as the fan-out step : 
 Steps before the fan-out run once. 
 The fan-out step returns a list of work items. 
 Every later main-line step runs once per item, which makes it the join. 
 Branch steps run per item too, only for the branches that item selected. 
 A workflow may have at most one fan-out step and it has to be on the main line. This is checked at save time, so a definition that cannot run says so while you are looking at it and not at 03:00 when the scheduler fires. 
 The admin UI draws the whole thing from the definition, including changes you have not saved yet: 

 That is gmail-triage, the most complex shape I run. mail-reader fans out over the unhandled messages, each item goes to arc1-specialist or sap-docs-specialist depending on what it is, then mail-draft-writer joins them into one draft reply. 
 Most workflows are simpler than that. The one I use below, sap-config-baseline , is three steps on the main line with no fan-out at all. 
 Branches and steps 

 A branch is a key and a description. The description is not documentation, it is prompt: the fan-out step gets the branch list appended to its instructions, with the rule to name only the branches an item actually needs. 
 A step is an agent, an instruction, an optional branch and a timeout. No branch means main line. Tick Fan-out step and it becomes the one that discovers the items. 
 A step does not have to be an agent though. Next to agent there are four deterministic kinds that run without a model: 
 condition : rules over the text, the item or a JSON field, with continue or stop as the outcome. 
 transform : extract a JSON path, run a regex, render a template, truncate. 
 http : call an endpoint through a BTP destination. 
 python : admin-authored code in a subprocess. 
 They take the previous step’s text and hand plain text on, exactly like an agent step does, so you can drop one anywhere in the line. Templates know {{text}} , {{item.<path>}} , {{json.<path>}} and {{source.<name>}} , substituted and never evaluated, there is no expression language to get clever with. 
 The screenshot above is sap-config-baseline : an agent reads the configuration out of the system, a python step scores it against the baseline, an agent writes the report. Step 2 is the deterministic one: 

 A kind, a timeout and a code field. Scoring a parameter against an expected value is not a judgement call, so it does not go through a model. Note the timeout as well: 60 seconds for the code against 600 for each agent around it. 
 That is the part I would not want to give up. The model is there for judgement. Everything that is a rule stays a rule. 
 The instruction on the step is the task, the agent’s own instructions are the expertise. That separation is what lets the same sap-docs-specialist sit in a branch here and answer questions in the chat, without either knowing about the other. 
 Between steps the handoff is plain text, one ## From <agent> block per predecessor and then the task. No schema, no field mapping. This felt wrong when I built it and has been right ever since, models are good at reading a previous agent’s answer and bad at filling in someone else’s JSON. 
 Settings worth knowing 

 API slug : the panel shows the endpoint it produces, which is the second scheduler entry point from the previous post. 
 Run as principal : fallback identity for steps whose agent has none. 
 Max parallel items : how many items run at once. Branches within one item always run sequentially, concurrent branches would just multiply load on the target system. 
 Skip items already seen : an item completed by an earlier run is skipped, so a retry after a crash resumes instead of re-drafting. 
 On unknown branch : fail that item, or skip the branch and carry on. 
 Before anything executes, every agent the workflow can reach is checked: exists, enabled, built, has an identity and that identity holds a usable credential. The peer graph too, not just the step agents. That one came out of a real failure: a peer without a usable credential does not fail the delegation, it returns the sign-in prompt as its answer, the parent reads that as content and the step is recorded as success. With skip-items-already-seen on, that wrong outcome is then permanent. 
 When something does stop a run, the run list says which step and why: 

 Running it 
 Manually, or on a schedule with an HTTP job pointing at the workflow’s run endpoint. Either way the run lands in Workflow Runs with per-item counters rather than one status: 

 Total, succeeded, failed and skipped, because a workflow over twelve messages is rarely all good or all bad. A run with failures next to successes is recorded as partial , which is the honest answer. 
 Conclusion 
 The orchestrator and the workflow engine solve opposite halves of the same problem. In a chat you want the model to decide what comes next, because you don’t know what the next question is. In an unattended run you want a human to have decided that in advance, because nobody is there to notice when the model decides badly. 
 What surprised me is how little the agents had to change. A workflow doesn’t wrap them, it only says in which order they speak. 
 Contributions and feedback are welcome, the full source code is on GitHub: https://github.com/lemaiwo/btp-dynamic-multiagent-app

 Post 1, configuring agents: https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-members/agentic-ai-on-btp-configuring-code-based-agents-on-the-fly/ba-p/14488352

items.title: SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026: What's New in Employee Central Payroll
items.author: shaktibarath
items.text:
The 2H 2026 release brings 16 features to Employee Central Payroll, covering Payroll Control Center enhancements, new replication scenarios for the United States, Ukraine, Qatar and Kuwait, identity and authentication changes, Joule payroll agents, two deprecations you need to act on, and legal changes across 21 countries and regions. 
 Here is a detailed breakdown of every feature in this release. 
 Payroll Enhancements in the Latest People Profile 
 The latest People Profile receives a large set of card enhancements in this release, and three of them are directly relevant for EC Payroll customers. 
 Payroll Replication Details: The Go to Data Replication Monitor link on this card now passes the employee's user ID to the Data Replication Monitor. When the monitor opens, the Employee search filter is already populated with that user ID. Previously, the link opened the monitor without any context and you had to search for the employee again. 

 Pay Statements: Employees and administrators can now access pay statements and payroll information from a previous legal entity after an intercompany transfer within the same employment. Go to the Payroll category in People Profile, use the As of Date calendar to pick a date within the previous legal entity assignment, and the Pay Statements and Payroll Information links refresh to show data from that legal entity. Set the calendar back to Today to return to the current assignment. This restores parity with the legacy People Profile and comes from customer idea 359363 . 

 Links in Payroll Information: Eligible payroll links can now open inside the Employee Central frame, so users keep the Employee Central header and user details. The behavior depends on the link type: 
 Service links (11 in total) follow predefined behavior. Services 1, 2, 10 and 11 open in the same tab as standalone applications, and services 3 to 9 (ESS PDF forms) open in the same tab within the Employee Central frame. No configuration is needed. 
 URL links are controlled by the Open in New Tab checkbox in Payroll Unified Configuration or Manage Data. Leave it unchecked to open the link within the frame. 
 Infotype links are controlled in Manage Data > Payroll System Configuration. In the SAP System Configuration for the relevant country/region, set Open Infotypes and Payroll Control Center in a new tab to No. 
 This enhancement comes from customer idea 364703 . 
 Type: Changed | Classification: Major | Action : Recommended | Enablement : Customer configured 
 Prerequisite : Enable the Enable the latest Editing and History UI for Employee Central HRIS entities on Full Profile admin setting. 
 Identity Provisioning Service: Migration to Global User ID 
 The enhanced report RP_HRSFEC_IAS_USER_ALIAS_UPD lets you migrate all existing users to Global User ID authentication across Identity Authentication Service, Employee Central and EC Payroll. The report migrates the Employee Central username, Person GUID and the Identity Authentication Service user identifier to Global User ID. 
 You can restrict the run to specific users with the Username field, and the report has a Test Run mode. For people with multiple contracts (and therefore multiple usernames), select the checkbox Update Alias/Global User ID for user created for first active employment. The alias is not updated automatically when several employee IDs exist for one person, and the first active employment is the one used for authentication. 
 Also note that the User Creation report is deprecated and replaced by the Identity Provisioning Service job. Global User ID is now the standard identity key across the systems. If you read the 1H 2026 post, this is the natural next step after Global User ID support for SAML authentication, which was only available for new customers. 

 Type : Changed | Classification : Minor | Enablement : Customer configured 
 Prerequisite : Install the Synchronization HR Support Package delivered in November 2026. 
 New Composite Roles for Administrators and Employee Self-Service 
 EC Payroll based on SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA now delivers two pre-configured composite roles that give immediate access to Employee Self-Service features, including payslip viewing in Employee Central: 
 SAP_CLDPY_ECPAY_ESS_COMPOSITE for employees 
 SAP_CLDPY_ECPAY_ADM_COMPOSITE for administrators 
 Previously, you had to copy the composite role yourself before assigning it. The delivered roles reduce the risk of errors in role assignment. Your administrator still needs to generate the profiles for these roles in transaction PFCG. 
 Type : Changed | Classification : Minor | Enablement : Automatically on 
 New Composite Roles for Administrators and Employee Self-Service 
 EC Payroll based on SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA now delivers two pre-configured composite roles that give immediate access to Employee Self-Service features, including payslip viewing in Employee Central: 
 SAP_CLDPY_ECPAY_ESS_COMPOSITE for employees 
 SAP_CLDPY_ECPAY_ADM_COMPOSITE for administrators 
 Previously, you had to copy the composite role yourself before assigning it. The delivered roles reduce the risk of errors in role assignment. Your administrator still needs to generate the profiles for these roles in transaction PFCG. 
 Type : Changed | Classification : Minor | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Deprecation of Old OAuth Configuration for Pay Statement 
 In the Security Center, the OAuth configuration that used ecp and ecp_ess has been replaced with a new OAuth configuration based on X.509 certificates. The old configuration is being retired on this timeline: 

 Milestone 
 Date 

 End of Development 
 May 15, 2026 

 End of Maintenance 
 November 13, 2026 

 Deleted 
 November 12, 2027 
 After end of maintenance, SAP no longer fixes bugs or delivers patches for the old configuration. If your pay statement integration still uses ecp and ecp_ess, plan the switch to the certificate based setup now. Refer to Using OAuth 2.0 to Integrate Employee Central and Employee Central Payroll for the steps. 
 Type : Changed | Action : Required | Lifecycle : Deprecated | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Deprecation of Basic Authentication for Point-to-Point Employee Central Payroll 
 Basic Authentication for point-to-point (push) replication to EC Payroll reached end of maintenance on June 2, 2023. The deletion date has now been moved from November 20, 2026 to November 12, 2027 so that it matches the deletion date in the SAP SuccessFactors platform. SAP recommends moving to a more secure method such as certificate authentication. 
 Basic authentication is being removed across several areas, and the dates are not the same everywhere. These are the ones most likely to affect an EC Payroll landscape:

 For more background, see the community blog Deprecation of Basic Authentication for Employee Central/Employee Central Payroll Connections 2H 2026 . 
 Type : Changed | Action : Required | Lifecycle : Deprecated | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Payroll Control Center: Manage Payroll Activities 
 Payroll Control Center is once again one of the biggest areas in this release, with four separate features for the Manage Payroll Activities solution. As mentioned in the 1H 2026 post, this solution is only available on SAP S/4HANA HCM, and the release notes for all four features only reference the S/4HANA HR support package schedule . Note also that these four features are valid as of November 3, 2026, while most other features in this release are valid as of November 13, 2026. 
 Concurrent Employment Support: Payroll Control Center now supports concurrent employment, where one person holds more than one position at the same time. This is common in the public sector and in shared service setups. 
 When concurrent employment payroll is active, you can select employees by Person ID. Step configuration in Set Up Steps now accepts report variants that use the PNPCE logical database, and validation rules and analytics designers can use Person ID as the alert entity or entity type. Previously, this was not possible and customers had to rely on workarounds outside Payroll Control Center. 
 Keep in mind that concurrent employment must be localized per country/region version, so it is not available everywhere (see SAP Note 1245073 ). You also need to configure new validation rules, analytics designers and activity lists for it. 
 Type : New | Classification : Major | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Rerun Payroll Activities for an Employee Sub-selection: When you start a step of the Job category, a dialog now appears before the step runs. It lists the available options and the number of employees in scope for each: 
 Current Selection: the selection used last time 
 Manual Selection: a manually defined set of employees 
 Full Selection: all employees eligible for the step 
 Employees with Alerts: only employees who have alerts 
 A practical example: after Initiate Policies, 30 out of 100 employees have alerts. Once the master data is corrected for those 30, you can rerun the Run Payroll step for only those employees instead of everyone. You can also define your own options (for example, employees in match code W for productive payroll) in the step type configuration in the Configuration Workbench ( PYC_CONFIG_WORKBENCH ). 
 Type : New | Classification : Major | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Operational and Configuration Enhancements: A collection of smaller improvements driven by customer incidents and Influence ideas: 
 Notes can now be added to critical operations such as resolving an alert or locking activities and steps. For Resolve Alert, the note and the action are stored as one audit trail entry. 
 When an activity cannot start (for example, because the employee selection is empty), payroll managers now get a specific error message instead of a generic one. 
 In Set Up Steps, selection parameter values support multiple filter rows combined with OR logic, so you can mix ranges and exact values for wage types in one step. 
 Analytics designers have a new Custom content type where you can plug in your own UI5 component by its ID. 
 The Wage Type Reporter ( H99CWTR0 ) can now process test payroll results, so you can run variance checks between test and productive results. 
 Job step status is more accurate. The system now reads the job log, converts errors to a standard format and sets the step to error status, so the step must be confirmed manually. Previously, a step could show OK even when the job log had errors. 
 Validate Alert is available during the Monitoring phase without having to enable Event Handler on the activity. 
 New report Download Activity Audit Trail ( PYT_PA_AUT_DOWNLOAD ) downloads the audit trail for regular and archived recurrences, and Administer Payroll Activities ( PYT_ACTIVITY_LIST_ADMIN ) can now manage stuck shadow recurrences. 
 Type : Changed | Classification : Minor | Enablement : Automatically on 
 Stand-Alone Dashboards: You can now create a dedicated activity list for an executive dashboard that covers all employees in selected payroll areas, company codes, or other dimensions such as employee group and personnel area. The dashboards show real-time KPIs with filters by organizational dimension and time period. One dashboard compares test payroll results with productive results for the current period. items.title: Migrating to SAP IBP Harmonized Planning Area (I_SAPIBP2): Before Getting Started
items.author: Kavyanshi
items.text:
Earlier this year, SAP rolled out a comprehensive enablement program as part of the 2025–2026 migration strategy to ensure SAP IBP customers and partners confidently adopt the new Harmonized Planning Area (I_SAPIBP2), 
 SAP IBP’s HPA 2026 Strategy: Unified Planning and ... - SAP Community 
 With the release of the MOVE2H tool (2605 release), SAP can support migrating existing IBP customers with SAP7F or SAP7-based order-based planning areas to I_SAPIBP2. The blog below contains some of the important technical pre-requisites with important tips and FAQs to help you kick-start with your HPA migration journey (Brownfield) 
 SAP has developed a comprehensive Migration Guide specifically designed for customers moving from their existing OBP planning areas to the Harmonized Planning Area (HPA), which is currently available only to early adopter customers and will be generally available soon. 
 Pre-Requisites: Before Getting Started 
 1. Know Your Migration Path 
 Before anything else, it is critical to identify which planning area you are migrating from , as this determines the complexity and the steps involved: 

 2. RTI Setup — Critical If You Are on SAP7 with SDI 
 Start with the S/4HANA side first. S/4HANA system upgrades — service packs or specific support notes — may be required. As seen earlier, it can take a long time to setup for customers on older S/4HANA or ERP versions. Note 3106619 - SAP IBP Real-time integration - Notes for installation - SAP for Me describes which support packages or notes you need to implement, depending on your release. The linked report CIF_NOTE_IMPL_SUPPORT_IBP will help identifying necessary notes. 
 You can use a dummy planning area (an independent copy of I_SAPIBP2 planning area) as a target for the RTI integration profile, so you do not have to wait for the full migration to begin. 
 SAP provides a web-based application called CIAS (Cloud Installation Agent Support) that helps accelerate the setup of the Cloud Connector and all related connections as a kind of workflow. 
 Before starting with the migration make yourself familiar with the following information: 
 RTI Central Note: 3110007 - IBP Real-time Integration: Information/Restrictions - SAP for Me 
 3. Time Profile — The Most Critical Configuration Element 
 The time profile is one of the most important aspects of HPA migration. There are four specific areas related to the time profile to assess and resolve before proceeding: 
 Custom Time Profile Levels 
 Check your planning area's time profile for any custom (user-defined) levels — for example, a fiscal year structure or custom quarter definitions. 
 Additional Attributes on Time Profile Levels 
 Check whether your time profile levels have additional custom attributes assigned . You need to attach them to the target time profile BEFORE the migration as well. Plan for Future Merging of Planning Areas; Consider whether you plan to merge multiple planning areas (e.g., order-based and time-series-based) now or in the future. Define the time profile with the union of all levels from all planning areas that may eventually be harmonized. Adding levels later is not possible. Adding attributes to existing time profile levels can be done at any time, but it is recommended to do that BEFORE the migration and before you load any data into the target time profile. 
 Understand How Your Period IDs Were Created 
 The Period ID (a technical identifier for each time period) is used internally across planning views, filters, and all other objects. The migration tools currently assume a one-to-one mapping of Period IDs between source and target. If you are unsure how your time profile was originally created (SAP standard numbering, manual upload, custom job), download the time profile CSV from the Data Integration app and share it with SAP Product Management. 
 4. Assess Your CI-DS Integration Strategy 
 CI-DS (Cloud Integration Data Services) can continue to be used with HPA. However, there are important nuances to evaluate before migration: 
 The existing CI-DS extractors are built on the data model of SAPIBP1 . To continue using CI-DS with HPA, custom content would need to be copied and adjusted to the new data structure. 
 Alternatively, this migration is an opportunity to switch to Cloud Integration (CI, SAP's recommended technology), where SAP provides predefined data flows. 
 The choice between continuing with CI-DS and adopting CI is a strategic decision that involves both effort and long-term benefits. This decision should be made before the technical migration begins. 
 In Addition to the above prerequisites, it's helpful to review some frequently asked questions (FAQs) from the Early Adopter Care (EAC) program initiative. 

 Question 
 Answers 

 How can we raise access to the Migrate Configuration app for migration to an I_SAPIBP2-based planning area, as SAP Help states that this is currently an Early Adopter feature? 

 To get access to the migration tool, an incident must be raised via component SCM-IBP-CNF-M2F 

 Will CI-DS continue to work with HPA? Since CI-DS targets a specific planning area, do all CI-DS interfaces need to be modified? 
 Yes, CI-DS can continue with HPA, but existing CI-DS extractors are based on the SAPIBP1/SAP 7F data model. To use CI-DS with HPA, you must build your own content. Alternatively, use this migration as an opportunity to switch to SAP Cloud Integration (predefined data flows). 

 We are migrating from SAP 7F and already have RTI in place with custom planning levels in OBP. Do we need to recreate those custom objects for the new planning area? 
 No. All configurations — custom key figures, planning levels, attributes — are supported by the migration tool. Having RTI already in place will significantly accelerate the process. Some manual pre- and post-migration adjustments will be needed before the planning area activates 

 We migrated from SAP7 to SAP7F and now want to go to HPA. Do we need to predefine all future time profile-level attributes, or can they be defined later? 
 Time-profile-level attributes can be added later, but it is recommended to ad them before the migration. What cannot change is the structure and order of the time profile levels themselves (which determines the internal period ID numbering). 

 Does the existing HPA support subnetwork planning in OBP, or is that a future roadmap item? 
 Yes, subnetwork planning is currently available in OBP. The 2611 roadmap item is specifically for time series supply optimization — not OBP. 

 Does the migration guide/tool provide field-level mappings — specifically, old 7F attribute IDs mapped to their HPA counterparts? 
 Yes. The tool contains all mappings in table form. 

 Historical data/KPIs — is there an automated tool for preserving them, or is it manual? 
 No automated tool support for data migration. If KPIs are stored as key figures in the old planning area, with equivalent key figures in the target, set up a copy operator to copy data from the source to the target, with attribute mappings defined between the two planning areas. 

 Our SAP7F is a non-cached version. Do we need to manually update the data source for each key figure to use cached data? 
 For SAP standard SAP7F key figures: no change needed. Only custom key figures with non-standard external data sources that reference non-cached order key figures need manual updates after migration to point to the cached data source. 

 HPA has cached key figures built in — so we don't need to switch them on separately, right? (Are these the OKF Keyfigures?) 
 Correct. Cached order key figures are enabled by default in HPA. It is a one-way setting — you cannot revert from cached back to non-cached. 

 Can two different forecast key figures be assigned to two different planning levels (one at product-location-customer level, another at product-location level)? 
 Yes, technically. The allocation profile and forecast consumption profile configured per product determine which level the system reads for each product. If it worked in SAP7F, it would work in HPA . 

 Can we add custom attributes now to time series planning levels in an existing live HPA planning area that was set up for a different purpose? 
 Yes. Adding non-root attributes to an existing planning area is possible. 

 We have a live time series planning area and a live OBP planning area. The plan is to first migrate OBP, then merge time series 1.5–2 years later. Will that be possible? 
 It is on the roadmap. The key prerequisite today: the time profile in the HPA target must contain all time profile levels from both planning areas before the first migration, and it is recommended to contain all attribute then as well (not mandatory). 

 My migration app view looks different from what you are demonstrating, and I don't see the same grouped options 
 You are missing the new business catalog that enables the enhanced grouped UI. If access was requested some time ago, the catalog may not have been assigned. Raise an SAP support ticket to have the new business catalog enabled. With release 2608, it will be automatically available in all systems 

 If I made a mistake in the mapping, can I delete the profile, create a new one, and restart? 
 Yes. You can reuse an existing mapping profile in a new migration project or create a new one. However, only restart before making any manual adjustments to the target. If manual adjustments were already made and you re-run migration, those adjustments will be overwritten 

 We have an active RTI profile for SAP7F. Can we create a second RTI profile for the new HPA planning area while both connect to the same S4/ERP system simultaneously? 
 Yes. You need two different logical systems in S4 (SM59) — one per planning area. Inbound integration can run in parallel from the same ERP to both planning areas. Outbound integration must NEVER run from two planning areas simultaneously for the same data. Separate logical systems also help distinguish body logic between SAP 7F and HPA in your BADI development, as the data structure has changed and some BADI might need to be adjusted (e.g. on PDS). 

 With two integration profiles, will the data flows for each planning area be fully separated even if using the same source data? 
 Yes. Different change pointers, completely independent data flows, separated by planning area. 

 There are ~200 OSS notes required for RTI setup in ECC. Should those be implemented before CIAS setup, or can they go in parallel? 
 They can mostly go in parallel. For most systems not on very old ERP 6.0, ~95% of CIAS setup can proceed in parallel with note implementation 

 We have custom staging tables in SDI that contain transformed data feeding into EXT tables. Can we reuse those custom staging tables as data sources in RTI BADIs? 
 Yes. Custom Z tables or standard X tables can be used as sources in RTI BADI logic 

 I want to migrate content in stages (planning filters first, then analytics, etc.) while making changes to the target in parallel. Will re-running migration reset the target to the source state? 
 Yes. Re-running migration overwrites objects in the target. Make all changes in the source first, then migrate. Do not modify the target expecting those changes to survive a subsequent migration run 

 Does cross-planning-area (inter-planning-area) copy operator migration also work, or only within-planning-area ones? 
 Yes, inter-planning-area copy operators are also supported, with restrictions. Only copy 
 operators assigned to the source planning area (where the job is not executable from target) are supported 

 Roles and authorizations — if copy operators or application job templates get new IDs after migration, do the role assignments get migrated too, or need to be recreated? 
 Business roles are not touched by the migration. Any role referencing technical names of application job templates or copy operators must be manually updated 

 Does the migration support a

items.title: Stored Procedures, Task Chains, and the Reusability Problem in SAP Datasphere
items.author: XaviPolo
items.text:
This is not a question about AI or the latest viral trend. It's about a real-life, day-to-day problem. 
 When you're managing more than 200 data sources and need to orchestrate a large number of loads and objects, efficiency and reusability are not nice-to-haves, they're essential. 
 In our case, we need to execute a common process every time one of those 200 tables is loaded. The initial idea was to add a single Stored Procedure to each Task Chain. Unfortunately, while Stored Procedures are not blocking in SAP HANA, SAP Datasphere block them, causing the chains to fail. 
 The alternative of creating 200 different Stored Procedures that all execute exactly the same logic, simply to work around this Datasphere limitation, doesn't seem like a reasonable solution. 
 Any ideas? How is a fundamental and widely used pattern such as code reuse supposed to be implemented in Datasphere? Thanks in advance.

Bridges the gap between deterministic portals and AI-driven conversational discovery on BTP.

1.teaching_angle: Use to explain API composition patterns for agents: (1) design principle—expose APIs as agent tools, not just UI endpoints; (2) spec quality—OpenAPI versioning and schema rigor matter for agent tooling; (3) tool design—descriptions are prompts that steer agent behavior, so naming and documentation are functional, not incidental.

5.summary: This post argues that monolithic agents with many tools and long instructions are unreliable for unattended workflows and proposes workflows as the production pattern: sequences of specialized agents and deterministic steps (condition, transform, http, python) orchestrated via admin UI without redeploy. The architecture allows fan-out over work items, conditional branching, and deterministic logic alongside LLM-powered steps. Each step can use a cheaper model for simple tasks and reserve expensive models for judgment-heavy steps, improving cost and auditability.
key_points: Monolithic agents fail in unattended scenarios: wrong path decisions, retry loops, poor auditability, inefficient tool selection, unnecessary access, model cost per step

5.why_it_matters: Production unattended workflows demand reliability, auditability, and cost control—properties that chat-orchestrated agents cannot guarantee. This post articulates the architectural boundary: AI for judgment, code for rules. It legitimizes running logic without LLMs and provides a concrete pattern (fan-out/join, branches, mixed-type steps) that SAP teams can apply to incident triage, config validation, data reconciliation, and repetitive background tasks on BTP.

deep_dives.title: Building an MCP server from an OpenAPI spec in Integration Suite
deep_dives.explanation:
The blog creates an MCP server artifact in Integration Suite (Integration Cell runtime) via Design → Integration Packages → Add MCP Server. The connection type is HTTP Endpoint with an OpenAPI specification, uploaded as a file. The spec must be OpenAPI 3.0. The SuccessFactors spec from SAP Business Accelerator Hub is 2.0 (Swagger), so it has to be converted first.

The example covers the Company Car domain in OData v2, with three layers. Reference data is `AllowedModels`, `RecommendedVendors` and `LeaseServiceProvider`. Policy is `BenefitCompanyCar`. Employee transactions are `CompanyCarEnrollment` and `CompanyCarClaim`. Tool discovery yielded 12 tools. The MCP Configuration tab then lets you inspect Tools, Resources and Prompts, including their input and output schemas, and manage Policies. The virtual host path (for example `<Virtual Host>/sfsf`) decides where the endpoint is hosted.

The main lesson is that the tool description is what the agent reads when choosing a tool. The blog recommends natural-language descriptions over technical entity names. The same applies to your own OData services: poor `$metadata` and annotations will likely produce poor tools. The post does not cover ABAP-backed services, so that part is an inference.
key_concepts: MCP Configuration: Tools, Resources, Prompts, Policies

deep_dives.title: Deterministic steps vs LLM steps in agent workflows
deep_dives.explanation:
The workflow post defines step kinds. Agent steps have a model and a timeout (600s in the example). Deterministic steps are `condition` (rules with continue/stop), `transform` (JSON path, regex, template, truncate), `http` (via a BTP destination) and `python` (subprocess, 60s timeout in the example). The structure is a main line, at most one fan-out step that must sit on the main line, branches and a join.

Handoff is plain text. Templates use `{{text}}`, `{{item.<path>}}`, `{{json.<path>}}` and `{{source.<name>}}`, which are substituted with no expression language. Branches have a key and description, and the description is appended to the fan-out instruction as decision rules.

The example, sap-config-baseline, reads config, scores it against a baseline and writes a report. The scoring is a condition, not a judgment, so no LLM is needed. The rationale is reliability, auditability and cost: use cheap models for reading and expensive ones only where judgment is required.

post_drafts.text:
*Not every step in an agent workflow needs an LLM.*

A BTP post argues monolithic agents are unreliable when unattended: wrong paths, retry loops, poor audit trail, high cost.

Its pattern: a workflow with agent steps plus deterministic steps (condition, transform, http, python).
Example: scoring config against a baseline is a condition, not a judgment.

interview_questions.question: Why might an unattended agent workflow use deterministic steps instead of letting one agent handle everything?
interview_questions.answer: A single agent with many tools and long instructions can choose wrong paths, loop on retries, and is hard to audit. It also pays model cost on every step. Splitting into a workflow lets rule-based logic, such as comparing a score with a baseline, run as a condition or transform step with no LLM. That makes the outcome reproducible and traceable. Agent steps are kept for judgment, and cheaper models can handle simple reading tasks. The same principle applies in ABAP: do not put deterministic rules inside a non-deterministic component.

interview_questions.question: What determines how well an MCP server generated from an OpenAPI spec works with an agent?
interview_questions.answer: The agent selects tools using their names and descriptions, so these act as prompts. The blog recommends clear natural-language descriptions over technical entity names. Spec quality matters too: Integration Suite needs OpenAPI 3.0, so a 2.0 Swagger spec must be converted. Input and output schemas can be inspected in the MCP Configuration tab. Poorly documented operations lead to wrong tool choices, so documentation is functional rather than cosmetic.

interview_questions.question: How would you decide whether an API should be exposed to AI agents, and what guardrails would you require?
interview_questions.answer: Start with the long-tail case: questions that fixed UIs cannot answer but that existing APIs can. Expose read-oriented, well-described operations first, as in the Company Car example with its reference, policy and transaction layers [1]. Use the separate Policies control in the MCP configuration. For write operations, require human approval, as the CAP multi-agent example does [6]. Prefer deterministic workflow steps for rule checks and keep agent steps for judgment [5]. This is a design synthesis; the sources do not give implementation detail for approval gates.
